videos.title: The ENTIRE History of China: The Empire That Comes Back.
videos.description:
China fell apart into warring kingdoms, was split between rival dynasties, conquered by Mongols and Manchus, carved up by foreign powers and torn by civil war. And every time, it pulled itself back together. This history documentary covers the entire history of China, from the Yellow River, the Shang oracle bones and the First Emperor to the Ming, the Opium Wars, the People's Republic and China today.

videos.title: How Iran Survived Every Empire That Tried to Destroy It
videos.description:
Alexander burned its capital. The Arabs ended its empire. The Turks took its throne and the Mongols destroyed its cities. And every time, a few generations later, the conquerors were speaking Persian. This history documentary covers the entire history of Iran, from Elam and the Persian Empire of Cyrus the Great to the Islamic Revolution, the war of 2026 and Iran today.

videos.title: Why Is South Korea Rich While the North Stayed Poor?
videos.description:
When whales fight, the shrimp's back breaks. For two thousand years Korea has been the shrimp between China, the Mongols, Japan, Russia and America, and every empire that tried to swallow it is gone. This history documentary covers the entire history of Korea, from the Dangun legend and the dolmen builders to the Korean War, the Miracle on the Han River and Korea today.

videos.title: He Walked Around the World for 28 Years. He Just Got Home
videos.description:
On November 1st, 1998, a former British Army paratrooper from Hull set off from Punta Arenas, at the bottom of Chile, with a tent, a few hundred dollars, a cheap camera and a handcart he later called "The Beast". His rule: walk home to England with unbroken footsteps. No car, no train, no plane, and no going home until he arrived on foot. He planned to be back in twelve years.

videos.description:

On the way home the engine died: water had got into the petrol. They had no anchor, and the current carried them north-east into the open Pacific.

videos.title: Would You Have Stayed With the Van? | 12 Days Lost in Australia
videos.description:
In July 2025, Carolina Wilga, a 26-year-old backpacker from Germany, rolled her campervan in the remote bush north of Beacon, Western Australia. She hit her head, left the van with all her water, food and even her shoes, and walked into the outback. For 12 days nobody knew where she was. She survived 11 nights on rainwater from puddles, slept in a cave, and kept a promise to her mum, until a farmer found her waving on the side of a dirt road.
